clue.text: Beating beer, and possibly gin

parts.note: wallop is British slang for beer

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of gin may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A drinker's beer and perhaps a gin chaser on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating beer' reads as a drink that beats others, but 'Beating' is the definition; 'possibly' scrambles the spirit's name, and wallop is old British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A walloping is a thrashing, so it can stand for a beating.

clue.text: Top dramatist might show self-control

parts.note: Will Shakespeare, the leading playwright
might means power

explanation.surface: A leading playwright perhaps displaying restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is a noun here; the top dramatist is Shakespeare, known familiarly by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength of resolve to resist impulses is self-discipline.

clue.text: Knight didn't get a lot for this weapon

indicators.note: didn't get says the knight's name is missing a portion

parts.note: Sir Lancelot is the Arthurian knight

explanation.surface: A knight who missed out on plenty gets this arm instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't get' removes the second half of the Round Table knight's name; 'a lot' reads as 'much' but is the very letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is a classic medieval weapon.

clue.text: Little beasts get work on very big problems

parts.note: op, opus, is a work
OS stands for outsize, very big
sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Small animals tackle huge difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size label; the pieces OP, OS and SUMS join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: These American marsupials are small animals, little beasts.

clue.text: Associate eventually includes a Test opener

indicators.note: includes means the phrase for eventually holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: in time means eventually

indicators.note: opener points to the first letter of the word Test

explanation.surface: A colleague will in due course feature in a first cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts A and T ('Test opener') inside IN TIME, between M and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate can be a close friend or confidant.

clue.text: Beg £1,000, a new way to speculate

indicators.note: new says the gathered letters are made into a fresh order

parts.note: L stands for pound (libra) and M for a thousand

explanation.surface: Asking for a grand is a novel route to playing the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BEG, L (pound), M (thousand) and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a risk for money, betting or speculating, is to wager.

clue.text: About twice round a tropical tree

indicators.note: twice asks for the abbreviation for about to be written two times over

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Directions for walking twice round a tree in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles CA, the abbreviation of circa (about), and O for 'round' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical American tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Wet and sticky for a short distance in the pipe

indicators.note: in places the small measure inside the word for pipe

parts.note: a clay is a clay tobacco pipe
mm, millimetre, is a short distance

explanation.surface: Damp gunk just a little way along a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts a millimetre inside an old-fashioned tobacco pipe made of fired earth; 'pipe' suggests plumbing, matching 'Wet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp and sticky to the touch describes clammy hands or weather.

clue.text: Impudence shown by expert with article on shrimps, etc

parts.note: crust is slang for cheek or impudence
an ace is an expert
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cheeky expert writes an article about shrimps and their kin.
explanation.walkthrough: The slang sense of impudence is British (as in 'a bit of a crust'); 'shown by', 'with' and 'on' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimps, crabs and lobsters belong to the hard-shelled class of arthropods.

clue.text: American playwright dotes on cooking

indicators.note: cooking, like cooking the books, means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A US dramatist loves to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on cooking' rearranges DOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford Odets wrote the 1930s US dramas Waiting for Lefty and Golden Boy.

clue.text: Jumpers seen at Twickenham?

parts.note: players leaping for a ball thrown in from touch at a rugby ground, not woollen pullovers

explanation.surface: A question about sweaters spotted in the crowd at a famous stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is England's national rugby union ground; at a throw-in from touch the forwards form a row and jumpers leap for the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the restart from touch is a formation where players jump for the thrown ball.

clue.text: Same members changed river enactment

indicators.note: the component letters of the word same are changed around into a new order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Unchanged legislators alter a river bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members changed' means the component letters of 'Same' rearranged; the river is a Yorkshire one, and 'enactment' is the parliamentary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is a law or act passed by a legislature, which is an enactment.

clue.text: The crowd before the Nazis ?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A history question about the crowds of pre-war Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before the Nazis' looks like a historical period, but it is a Latin prefix followed by Hitler's paramilitary force's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a dense throng of people pushing together, a crowd.

clue.text: Eskimo dogs-do only the bitches berk?

definitions.meaning: sled dogs of the Alaskan Inuit breed
a whimsical question implying the boys of the pack stay silent; berk stands for bark as printed

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'berk', clearly meaning 'bark': if only the bitches bark, the dogs of the other sex are silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute is a large Alaskan sled dog, and the second part suggests silent male hounds.

clue.text: Job's communion?

parts.note: fellowship found in one's employment, not the biblical patriarch's religious rite

explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like the biblical figure but means employment; the companion there is a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a companion at one's job, so comradeship in employment suggests one.

clue.text: Mnemonic includes key for the rest

indicators.note: includes means the memory aid holds the musical key inside it

parts.note: a reminder is a mnemonic
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A memory aid containing a key clue to what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' places A, a musical key, inside REMINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the remainder, the rest.

clue.text: Mark causes endless alarm

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for alarm is dropped

parts.note: a scare is a sudden alarm

explanation.surface: A blemish that keeps on causing worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the last letter off SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Parish overseer from a forest in the country

parts.note: rural means of the countryside
the Forest of Dean is in Gloucestershire

explanation.surface: A parish supervisor coming out of a woodland in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Dean is an ancient woodland in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England cleric supervising a group of parishes.

clue.text: Bright decoration servant put up before

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word for servant is read upwards

parts.note: a maid is a servant
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A servant hangs up a shiny ornament beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the servant in this down clue; the Latin for 'before' follows, as in ante-room.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering sequin or paste trim on clothing gives a sparkly ornament.

clue.text: A place the better types would leave

definitions.text: A place the better types would leave

parts.words: A place the better types would leave
parts.note: a building patients depart once they have recovered and are feeling improved

explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as superior people but means those recovered from illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients are discharged from the medical ward when they get well.

clue.text: Epstein's work an eastern prince returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for the prince is written backwards

parts.note: an amir (or emir) is a Muslim ruler or prince

explanation.surface: A sculptor's piece given back by an oriental royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AMIR backwards. Jacob Epstein's carving of Rima, from W H Hudson's novel Green Mansions, stands in Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Rima is a well-known relief sculpture by Jacob Epstein, a memorial to the naturalist Hudson.

clue.text: Sound IRA revolutionary, this creature

indicators.note: revolutionary hints at turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sound sounding as if it came from a rebel paramilitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges SOUND and IRA together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a prehistoric reptile, the beast the clue points at.

clue.text: One and one a side

definitions.meaning: the digits 1 and 1 side by side make the number following ten
a cricket or football team has that many players

explanation.definitionFit: Written as figures, two ones make the number; it is also a full football or cricket team.

clue.text: Writer to disregard Polonius's advice

definitions.meaning: Polonius in Hamlet counsels 'neither a borrower nor a lender be'

explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow was a Victorian travel writer; taking a loan ignores Polonius's counsel.

clue.text: Third degree restaurant ?

parts.note: an eatery imagined as the place for harsh police questioning, since such questioning is a word for cooking under a hot element

explanation.walkthrough: Giving someone the third degree is interrogating them hard, also called grilling; the eating place is named the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining room specialising in broiled meats takes its name from the cooking method that also means interrogation.

clue.text: Drug commonly swallowed by lower types?

definitions.meaning: cattle that low eat it on the common

explanation.definitionFit: Marijuana is slang called weed; it is also what cattle graze on common land.

clue.text: Rose's adherent departed quietly — returning

indicators.note: returning means the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the late are the departed, the dead
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A follower of Rose slipped off quietly, only to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses LATE plus P, giving the run backwards. 'adherent' looks like a follower but is something stuck to the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf of the flower clings to its head, an adherent part of the rose.

clue.text: Some card ! But a jolly good fellow

definitions.meaning: a card of the suit ranking above the others
dated slang for a splendid, reliable person

explanation.definitionFit: A winning suit card beats others; old slang also used the word for a thoroughly decent chap.

clue.text: Breathless footpad's demand in Hampshire town

indicators.note: breathless means losing the h, the breathy aspirate sound

parts.note: a highway robber demands that you give up your valuables

explanation.surface: A panting robber holds up a victim in a southern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: A footpad is an old word for a robber on foot whose cry is 'Hand over!'; 'Breathless' drops the H (an aspirate). Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a market town in the county of Hampshire, England.

clue.text: Japanese ornament Sue Kent mislaid

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the names are put down wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sue Kent has lost her Japanese trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' rearranges SUE and KENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved toggle worn on a kimono sash, a Japanese ornament.

clue.text: Fascinating woman warned of attack?

definitions.meaning: a seductress, like the singing temptresses of Greek myth
the wartime alarm that wailed before an air raid

explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is called this after the mythic singers; it is also the alarm sounding before air raids.

clue.text: Direction to cads — taking peg is bad for driving

parts.note: W, west, is a compass direction
heels are cads, bounders
a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: Advice to rogues that pinching pegs will spoil their motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction to cads' sounds like an order to bounders, but it is a compass point followed by a slang word for cads; 'taking' adds the peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning the tyres without grip wastes power and is poor motoring technique.
